subject: Can truncation limits of a normal distribution be vectorized?

messages.author: 33d5534e21fbbe0f
messages.subject: Can truncation limits of a normal distribution be vectorized?
parts:
if I have a vector of parameters, t, under a truncated normal, i interpret the manual to indicate that one may not specify upper and lower limits in a vectorized form.   I also can't get around this by directly updating lp__ using normal_cdf, since such is also not vectorized.   Is this correct?

--
Thank you, Terrance Savitsky

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can truncation limits of a normal distribution be vectorized?
parts:
On 9/21/12 9:39 PM, terrance savitsky wrote:
> if I have a vector of parameters, t, under a truncated normal, i interpret the manual to indicate that one may not
> specify upper and lower limits in a vectorized form. I also can't get around this by directly updating lp__ using
> normal_cdf, since such is also not vectorized. Is this correct?

No, I'm afraid that truncated normals can't be vectorized,
nor can normal_cdf.

We might add normal as a special case eventually after
we've vectorized the other basic probability functions.
We already have a truncated_normal_log() floating around
waiting to be vectorized.

- Bob
